title: AI-assisted drone helps rescuers find two overdue hikers
date_precision: Reported overdue June 23, 2026; exact rescue date unreported. Official account published June 25, 2026.
location: Dead Horse Gap walking track, near Jindabyne, New South Wales, Australia
system: Fire and Rescue NSW drone with AI detection software and thermal camera; model and vendor not identified.
observed_outcome: Both hikers were located and guided to safety.
ai_contribution: The agency attributes initial identification in the bush to the drone's AI software; thermal imaging confirmed the find.
human_contribution: The drone operator confirmed the find using thermal imagery and used a spotlight to guide Police and State Emergency Service rescuers. The hikers also signaled with a phone light.
evidence_type: Official operational report; no independent causal evaluation.
evidence_supports: A first-party operational account describes identification, confirmation, and rescue.
limitations: The report does not isolate AI's contribution from thermal imaging, the hikers' signal, or rescuers. It does not establish injuries or deaths avoided, or time saved.
tradeoffs: No adverse effects are reported; costs, surveillance implications, and false detections are not evaluated.
replication_hypothesis: Test whether trained operators, effective imaging, ground-team coordination, and clear confirmation procedures enable similar rescues.

title: AI fire alert precedes the first 911 call near Grass Valley
date_precision: Day and local alert time explicitly reported.
location: Near Grass Valley, California, United States
system: ALERTCalifornia camera network and DigitalPath/CAL FIRE fire-detection AI.
observed_outcome: AI alerted at 5:19 a.m.; firefighters were on scene before the first 911 call at 6:01 a.m. The fire remained under a quarter acre.
ai_contribution: Detected a possible ignition in the Wolf Mountain 1 camera feed and alerted firefighters.
human_contribution: The program uses trained watchstanders to confirm detections. Firefighters responded and contained this fire.
evidence_type: First-party program report; no independent causal evaluation.
evidence_supports: The university operating the camera program reports the alert, first-call times, and final containment.
limitations: Earlier notification and containment are observed. A larger fire, specific losses, or casualties avoided are not established. The comparison is with the first 911 call, not every possible detection route.
tradeoffs: No event-specific adverse effects are reported; false alarms, response costs, and surveillance effects are not evaluated.
replication_hypothesis: Test whether camera coverage, human confirmation, reliable dispatch, and available crews produce earlier effective responses elsewhere.
beneficiaries: Nearby residents and property were the intended beneficiaries; specific losses avoided are unmeasured.
sources: [{"title": "ALERTCalifornia and CAL FIRE's Fire Detection AI Program Named One of TIME's Best Inventions of 2023", "url": "https://today.ucsd.edu/story/alertcalifornia-and-cal-fires-fire-detection-ai-program-named-one-of-times-best-inventions-of-2023", "publisher": "UC San Diego", "published": "2023-10-24", "type": "First-party program report"}]

title: Incidental lung cancer diagnosed before planned anti-TNF treatment
date_precision: study period; individual episode dates unreported
location: Turkey/India multicenter study; individual center unreported
observed_outcome: A 57-year-old man received a stage IB lung adenocarcinoma diagnosis and underwent right upper lobectomy.
ai_contribution: Flagged a lung nodule on a chest X-ray obtained before anti-TNF treatment for ulcerative colitis.
human_contribution: Clinicians confirmed the finding, pursued imaging and biopsy, and performed surgery.
evidence_type: Individual episode within a peer-reviewed five-patient case series
evidence_supports: Documents detection, diagnosis, and treatment for Case 1.
limitations: No comparator or long-term follow-up; survival benefit unestablished. AstraZeneca funded the study; one author worked for Qure.ai.
tradeoffs: False flags can trigger unnecessary investigations. Accuracy and net benefit cannot be estimated from these selected cases.
replication_hypothesis: Clinician review, accessible confirmatory testing, and reliable treatment referrals.
intendedness: Intended diagnostic support; finding incidental to the original care plan.
source_case_identifier: CREATE case series, Case 1 (one of five; same study)

title: AI-prioritized X-ray followed by stage I lung cancer diagnosis
observed_outcome: Dianne Covey was contacted about an abnormality the afternoon of her X-ray; further investigation identified stage I lung cancer.
ai_contribution: Flagged the X-ray for urgent clinical review.
human_contribution: Her GP referred her; hospital staff interpreted findings, contacted her, and investigated.
evidence_supports: Describes an AI-assisted care sequence and an early-stage diagnosis.
limitations: No clinical record or comparison is supplied. Treatment and longer-term outcomes are unreported. Does not establish that AI changed cancer stage or saved her life.
tradeoffs: No case-specific harms are reported; broader false-positive rates and workflow costs are unmeasured here.
replication_hypothesis: Prompt review, patient contact, and capacity for follow-up diagnostics.
beneficiaries: One patient described in a public hospital account.

title: Recovery after stroke treatment supported by AI imaging
location: Royal Sussex County Hospital, Brighton, United Kingdom
observed_outcome: Carol Wilson underwent clot-removal surgery, returned home within two days, and reported resuming work, exercise, and childcare.
ai_contribution: The hospital identifies her care as an example of its AI-supported stroke imaging and coordination pathway; case-specific AI timing is unreported.
human_contribution: Emergency responders transported her; clinicians diagnosed the stroke and performed thrombectomy.
evidence_supports: Reports treatment and recovery in an AI-supported pathway.
limitations: No comparator or detailed alert log. The account cannot isolate AI's contribution from rapid emergency response, surgery, or other care.
tradeoffs: No case-specific AI harms are reported. Missed alerts, false flags, and resource costs are not evaluated.
replication_hypothesis: Immediate emergency assessment, connected stroke teams, and timely access to thrombectomy.
beneficiaries: One patient described in a public hospital account.
sources: [{"title": "East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust (2021)", "url": "https://www.esht.nhs.uk/2021/09/07/cutting-edge-technology-benefits-stroke-patients/", "type": "primary institutional account", "published": "2021-09-07"}]
